text:
maya: FYI I pushed raven-lite-int4-v2 to staging for the toolcall onboarding run, ran the 10k canary suite. parse_success_rate dropped from 99.4% (fp16) to 90.2% on the same prompt set.
kevin: ouch, that's bigger than I expected. any pattern in failures?
sasha: quick dump: 120 failures sampled -> most are truncated arrays or trailing commas, plus some non-json narratives. attaching examples below.
maya: sample snippets: ```
1) {
  "action": "update_ticket",
  "params": [
    {"id": 123, "note": "triage done"}
  ]
  // missing closing brace due to eos token
```
```
2) {
  "tool": "calculate",
  "args": "[1,2,3]"
  "result": 6

```
kevin: looks like tokenization/quant noise causing early cutoffs and sometimes quoting issues. what's the generation config?
maya: used onboard default: temp=0.2, max_tokens=160, streaming enabled, kv-prefix enabled, batch-size 16. quant profile = int4-squeeze (our new PTQ).
eli: did we compare sampling seeds vs fp16? maybe topk/top-p got nudged by quantization.
sasha: ran a deterministic regen (seeded) on 500 failing prompts — 62% still fail under int4, 95% pass on fp16 using identical seeds. so it's not just sampling randomness.
kevin: could be attention kernel rounding on long JSON tails. any correlation with sequence length?
maya: yes: > 380 tokens in prompt+response -> failure rate jumps to 18%. short ones <200 tokens are ~95% success.
ci-bot: new staging run finished: metrics: parse_success_rate=90.2%, median_latency=210ms, 95p_latency=520ms, retry_count_avg=0.08. artifacts at https://ci.internal/runs/1718301234/artifacts
eli: good. propose temporary mitigations: (1) increase max_tokens margin to 240, (2) add postprocess JSON healer that attempts to close braces/trailing commas and detect string escapes, (3) run small canary with 1% traffic and mirror fp16 in shadow for parity.
sasha: about (2) — we already have a json_repair heuristic in the eval harness; it recovers ~40% of failures but some toolcall contracts require strict arrays/types so repair isn't always safe. we should log repaired vs raw.
kevin: also try lowering kv-prefix batching for these runs (disable prefix concat) — I've seen prefix truncation cause array fragmenting in other models.
maya: I'll spin three experiments: A) int4 with max_tokens 240, B) int4 + postprocess healer, C) int4 with prefix disabled. each run 5k prompts. schedule for tomorrow morning.
eli: add explicit schema prompts (assert types) as a soft constraint in the prompt template and supply <SCHEMA> token to encourage well-formed json. may help.
sasha: note for onboarding checklist: add parse_success_rate delta compared to fp16, long-tail length bucketed analysis, and per-contract repair rate. I'll update the onboarding template.
kevin: if A/B/C still under target (>98% success), we should fallback to fp16 auto for structured endpoints (policy that routes to a higher-precision variant when parse fails more than X%).
maya: agreed. i'll collect the three runs and post the quick diff. tagging @kevin @sasha for the canary watch.
ci-bot: experiment jobs queued: job/1718302000 (A), job/1718302100 (B), job/1718302200 (C). will post results here when done. :rocket:
kevin: thanks — also remind infra to reserve a tiny dedicated slot for deterministic regen (we need same env for seeds).
eli: can someone add a small eval that specifically checks for trailing-comma and unclosed-brace errors and surfaces token positions? that'll help kernel team.
maya: will do. closing loop when runs finish.
